# Campaign and Intrusion Analysis Report

Type 5 · Operational and incident · `campaign-intrusion-analysis` · ID prefix `PG-CAMP-`

The complete account of one campaign or intrusion set: when it ran, whom it targeted, how it worked end to end, the infrastructure and tools behind it, who is likely responsible, and what to change.

**Use it when:** After an alert has been worked, or when an intrusion set has enough evidence for a full account. Attribution here is a judgment; the ACH Attribution Matrix holds the test behind it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Audience | Incident response leads, Threat hunters, SOC leadership |
| Tier | Operational |
| Default marking | TLP:AMBER · PAP:AMBER |
| Valid for | 90 days from issue |
| Formats | markdown, json, stix |
| Suggested for PIRs | Threat actor and campaign tracking (operational); Third-party and supply-chain risk (operational); Brand, VIP, and digital-footprint protection (operational) |
| Related types | [Threat Activity Alert](threat-activity-alert.md), [ACH Attribution Matrix](ach-attribution-matrix.md), [ATT&CK Navigator Layer](attack-navigator-layer.md), [Detection Signature Bundle](detection-signature-bundle.md), [Infrastructure Clustering Graph](infrastructure-clustering-graph.md) |

## Sections

In order. A required section with no content makes the report **Incomplete**, and the report names it. Every report has the header, the PIR verdict, Gaps and Limitations, and Sources.

| # | Section | Required | Provenance | Built from |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Report header (`header`) | yes | Method | ReportIssue, reports/contract.py |
| 2 | Priority intelligence requirement (`pir_verdict`) | yes | Method | AnalyticInvestigation, reports/pir.py |
| 3 | Threat summary (`threat_summary`) | yes | Model draft + Analyst | report section text, report severity |
| 4 | Key judgments (`key_judgments`) | yes | Analyst + Model draft | analytic ledger assertions and hypotheses |
| 5 | Campaign timeline (`campaign_timeline`) | yes | Evidence + Method | observation first- and last-seen fields, campaign claims |
| 6 | Victimology (`victimology`) | yes | Evidence + Analyst | actor claims (targets-sector, targets-region) |
| 7 | Attack narrative (`attack_narrative`) | yes | Model draft + Analyst + Method | Kill Chain mappings, ATT&CK mappings, report section text |
| 8 | Infrastructure (`infrastructure_breakdown`) | yes | Evidence | STIX objects, role tags, investigation graph, observations |
| 9 | Arsenal and tooling (`arsenal`) | yes | Evidence + Analyst | actor claims (uses-malware, uses-tool), file observations |
| 10 | ATT&CK techniques and procedures (`attack_matrix`) | optional | Evidence | accepted framework mappings, pinned ATT&CK Enterprise v19.2 |
| 11 | Recommendations (`recommendations`) | yes | Analyst | report recommendations |
| 12 | Indicators of compromise (`ioc_table`) | yes | Evidence | STIX objects |
| 13 | Detection and hunt pointers (`detection_pointers`) | optional | Method | issued reports |
| 14 | Gaps and limitations (`gaps_limitations`) | yes | Method + Analyst | lifecycle knowledge_gap and limitation items, element results |
| 15 | Sources (`sources`) | yes | Method | module runs |

## What each section must say

- **Report header.** Report ID, version, status, marking, audience, requirement, validity and producer.
- **Priority intelligence requirement.** The question, its category and tier, and the deterministic verdict (DEC-PIR-001).
- **Threat summary.** The campaign in three sentences - period, victims, objective - and the main defensive takeaway.
- **Key judgments.** Attribution and objective, each with likelihood, separate confidence and basis; reference the ACH matrix if one was issued.
- **Campaign timeline.** First and last observed activity from source-reported dates (not collection times), and dated events.
- **Victimology.** Targeted sectors and regions, each with its basis and citations.
- **Attack narrative.** Phase by phase from initial access to actions on objectives, each step with ATT&CK IDs and citations. State gaps; do not bridge them.
- **Infrastructure.** Each domain, address and URL with its role tag, hosting or ASN, connections and source count.
- **Arsenal and tooling.** Malware families and tools used in this campaign, with capability and first and last use.
- **ATT&CK techniques and procedures.** Tactic, technique ID and name, and the observed procedure, from accepted mappings against the pinned release.
- **Recommendations.** Remediation and hardening steps, each with an owner and due date, in priority order.
- **Indicators of compromise.** The campaign's full indicator set; the JSON and STIX renderings are the machine-readable appendix.
- **Detection and hunt pointers.** Issued detection bundles, hunting packages and Navigator layers for this investigation.
- **Gaps and limitations.** Recorded knowledge gaps and limitations, plus every element that came back empty or partial.
- **Sources.** Every collection source that ran, with run and object counts and its Admiralty rating.

## Rules every report follows

- Indicator values are defanged in Markdown and unchanged in JSON, STIX and rule files.
- Each judgment states a likelihood term and, separately, a confidence level ([vocabularies](README.md#vocabularies)).
- Each section shows its provenance; each source shows its Admiralty rating.
- Examples use reserved names and addresses only (RFC 2606, RFC 5737, RFC 3849).
